evidence: The hunk's comment literally says "golangci-lint at v2.8.0 in ci.yml", a second copy of a value ci.yml owns and invites bumping; the agent replaced it with "ci.yml pins golangci-lint" and also swept the same-defect "36 gofmt-dirty files" count, while rightly leaving the frozen CHANGELOG literal alone.
guidance_note: When a comment explains why a pinned value matters, state that the pin exists and where it lives, never the pinned literal itself.

narrative: One comment-drift finding about a hardcoded version literal in .golangci.yml. The agent fixed it, swept a second literal of the same kind in the same comment, and declined to touch the frozen CHANGELOG with a stated reason. Round 1 approved with nothing new.
guidance_observations: Fixing the class (the drifting file count) alongside the cited literal prevented a likely second round.

evidence: The table's own doc comment claims it pins every cell of verb x lane shape (6 cells) while the hunk holds only takeover rows for the named lane; the agent confirmed 4 of 6 and added solo+abandoned and default-lane+abandoned, which surfaced a real "take over it" grammar defect.
guidance_note: When a test comment or CHANGELOG claims a full product of cases is pinned, count the rows against the product before pushing; the agent's own mutation run used a -run filter that excluded the covering file.

evidence: F1's fix commit cf1926c rewrote startAdvice to spell out four sentences and added the comment "All four are pinned as the product of verb and lane shape", while the same fix made the table pin six cells; the number in the new comment conflated templates with cells.
guidance_note: When a fix writes a comment that states a count, re-derive the number from the code and tests the same commit changed rather than from the shape just refactored.

evidence: The reviewer notes the ServedFromEpicLane suffix "(a second lane of an epic you already hold a lane in)" was introduced by the original diff and pinned in next_test.go, yet the rewritten doc sections present only the two bare sentences as the output spec; this is original-PR scope, not fix-caused.
guidance_note: When rewriting a doc section that enumerates a command's output lines, grep the renderer for every variant's string and check each appears in the enumeration.

evidence: next_route.go:322 passes takeoverWork into step 2's pick, so ServedFromEpicLane can carry an abandoned row, and the renderer table's only ServedFromEpicLane case used a fresh row; this is the same verb-x-shape coverage gap F1 named, left unswept on the renderer when F1's fix reverted the renderer rows, as the agent itself says ("the same class as the gap the previous round caught").
guidance_note: When a coverage finding names a missing cell of a product, enumerate every site that composes the same product (here the renderer's suffix concatenation) and pin the takeover cell there too.

evidence: The step-1b overlap is real (gatingDependencies resolves deps from the full byID set), but keying the qualifier to the routing step is a defensible design; the actual defect was F3's fix eebecc0 writing cli-reference as "A pick that continues an epic you already hold a lane in closes on a qualifier", a fact-framed claim false for step 1b, which the agent corrected to step-scoped wording.
guidance_note: When a doc fix describes when a line appears, phrase the condition in the same terms the code branches on (the routing step), not the fact the line happens to state.

narrative: The PR renames claim announcements into conditional start advice. F1's coverage fix introduced a comment miscounting cells (F2), and its revert of the renderer rows left the epic-continuation takeover cell unpinned (F4). F3's doc fix stated the qualifier as a fact rather than a step, which F5 caught alongside a real but defensible design overlap. The fifth round hit the review cap and went unreviewed.
guidance_observations: Two of the agent's own claims were wrong because a mutation check was run with a -run filter that excluded the covering tests; whole-package mutation runs would have avoided the false conclusion.
Each fix touched prose (a comment or doc line) that stated counts or conditions, and each one drew the next round; re-reading new prose against the code before pushing was the missing step.
The round cap was reached with the last push (81c45db) unreviewed.

evidence: NoWork{Unreachable: passedOver(rows, reachFor)} can hold the whole filtered backlog and was joined uncapped, so the edge case is real; the reviewer's implied existing capping convention does not exist (describeIDSet is deliberately uncapped for forensic reasons), which the agent noted while capping in the shared describeReach with an explicit "and N more" count.
guidance_note: When widening a diagnostic's input from a scoped set to an unbounded one, decide its rendering bound in the same change.

narrative: One edge-case finding about an unbounded id list in the NoWork diagnostic. The agent corrected the reviewer's false claim of an existing convention, capped in the single shared renderer with an explicit remainder count, and mutation-tested both the unbounded join and silent truncation. Round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: Placing the cap in the shared renderer rather than the flagged call site covered Exhausted as well and avoided a follow-on finding.

evidence: Satisfied() was `e.Target == e.State`; AllOf.State() returns InProgress for any partial epic and Open as a childless fallback, so start on a partial epic and open on a childless one both exited 6 "nothing to do"; the agent reproduced 0-of-2 exiting 6 live and added Total > 0 && Unfinished() == 0.
guidance_note: Before writing an equality predicate over a derived state, tabulate every input shape x action and check which cells the equality admits; the enumeration would have shown three false 'satisfied' cells.

evidence: Same root cause as F1: AllOf.State() returns Closed first when Closed == Total, so InProgress implies Unfinished() > 0 and start-satisfied was wrong every time it fired; fixed by the same Satisfied() change in 0b87f60.
guidance_note: Write sweep tests that assert the exact reason and exit code per cell, not just negative properties both branches satisfy.

evidence: The new Error() interpolates e.State with raw %s, leaking "in_progress" into prose although State.Display() is documented for human-readable messages; the agent switched both interpolations and pinned presence of "in progress" and absence of "in_progress".
guidance_note: When interpolating a domain enum into user-facing text, check whether the type has a designated display renderer before using %s.

narrative: Round 0 found a real logic defect in the new Satisfied() predicate (F1 and F2 are duplicates of one root cause) plus a wire-format leak into prose (F3). The agent reproduced both live, fixed Satisfied() with conjuncts expressing the domain fact, replaced the weak sweep test with a sixteen-cell table, and mutation-verified it. Round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: The original sweep test exercised the broken cell on every run but asserted only properties both branches satisfied; a table of exact expected outcomes in the original PR would have caught the defect before review.
The fix enumerated a fourth action (close) neither reviewer listed, avoiding the same enumeration hole one level up.
